verified_by: 3-state differential compile (Maven 3.9.11, JDK 11) on a clean clone of the client repo
why_excluded: The adaptation responds to a COMPILE-time (syntactic) breaking change, not a behavioural one. snakeyaml 2.0 kept an arity-1 `Constructor` but narrowed its parameter from `Class` to `LoaderOptions`, so the client's `new Constructor(ApplicationConfig.class)` does not compile against 2.0 at all. The client never observed a runtime behaviour change: the build simply stopped compiling. Syntactic BCs are out of scope for this dataset — the whole point is adaptations to breaks that survive compilation and only manifest at runtime.

discovery.note: This was the ONLY traversal-confirmed, production, native-Maven candidate left unverified across every mined corpus as of 2026-08-06. Its exclusion empties the verification queue.

adaptation.message: Fix Windows compatibility: Update SnakeYAML to v2.0 and add LoaderOptions support
adaptation.the_change: new Constructor(Foo.class) -> new Constructor(Foo.class, new LoaderOptions())
adaptation.summary: Bump snakeyaml 1.29 -> 2.0 and add the LoaderOptions argument that 2.0's Constructor requires. Bump and adaptation are in the same commit (shape: BUNDLED_BUMP_AND_ADAPTATION), which is itself a signal of a compile break: the author could not have committed the bump alone, because the tree would not build.

traversal.note: Rule 5 (boundary crossing) IS satisfied — the client genuinely crossed 1.x -> 2.0 in its own history. The case fails on the nature of the break, not on the crossing.

verification.method: 3-state differential using `mvn compile` (not test — the repo contains no src/test at all, so no Surefire differential is possible). Clean clone, snakeyaml version varied via pom.xml, Maven repo -Dmaven.repo.local=C:/bump-p4p/.bbc_m2, JDK 11 (pom sets java.version=11, Spring Boot 2.7.0 parent).

states.name: 2_new_lib_old_code
states.detail: YamlParserService.java:[23,66] incompatible types: java.lang.Class<com.example.dashboard.model.Application> cannot be converted to org.yaml.snakeyaml.LoaderOptions; same error at ApplicationConfigService.java:[25,72]

verification.conclusion: State 2 fails at javac, not at runtime. This is a syntactic breaking change and therefore NOT a BBC. The client's fix is a signature fix, not a behavioural adaptation.
verification.no_tests_in_repo: src/test does not exist at any commit in this repo, so even had the break been behavioural, the standard Surefire per-test differential could not have run. The compile differential was decisive on its own.

tooling_finding.issue: ARTIFACT HYGIENE, not a tool defect. screen_compile_break.py was already correct and had already excluded this row; the wrong verdict survives only in a stale upstream file.
tooling_finding.what_happened: The row was picked up from `..._traversal_RECHECK.jsonl` (written 2026-08-04 01:15), where its compile_screen reads 'behavioural' with reason 'all 6 library constructor usage(s) in the parent source still exist at 2.0'. That verdict was inherited from the arity-only screen run of 2026-08-04 00:06 and never refreshed in that file. The type-aware re-screen at 09:53 (`..._RECHECK_SCREENED.jsonl`) had ALREADY demoted this row to compile_break, and the downstream `..._TRIGGER.jsonl` correctly drops it.
tooling_finding.correct_reason: Constructor(java.lang.Class) has no matching overload at 2.0 (overloads: [['org.yaml.snakeyaml.LoaderOptions']])
tooling_finding.screen_reconfirmed_2026_08_06: Re-running the current screen over all 44 rows reproduces the 09:53 tally exactly — {compile_break: 10, behavioural: 33, unknown: 1} — and the per-row verdicts are byte-identical. The signature-narrowing check (`signature_mismatch_at_to_version`, which compares erased argument types against the to_version jar's overloads via javap) works as documented.
tooling_finding.real_implication: The `_traversal_RECHECK.jsonl` files are PRE-screen inputs that nonetheless carry a compile_screen field, so reading a candidate list from them yields verdicts that the pipeline has already superseded. The authoritative artifacts are `_SCREENED` and `_TRIGGER`. This naming trap cost a full manual verification cycle and should be fixed — either strip the stale field from RECHECK outputs or rename so the screening stage is unambiguous.
tooling_finding.value_retained: The javac differential above is the first EMPIRICAL confirmation of a screen_compile_break.py compile_break verdict — until now the screen's classifications were trusted on javap inspection alone. Its call here is exactly right.
